Based on assessment of balance and gait.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Exemplifying with NANDA: NANDA diagnoses related to the identified problems (Educational purpose)
Based on assessment of balance and gait.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Frequently Asked Questions
Follow more nursing information on our Nursing Forum.

Related Scales
Morse Fall Scale Fall risk assessment.

Berg Balance Scale Assessment of static and dynamic balance.

Katz ADL Scale Independence in activities of daily living (ADLs).

Scientific Reference
TINETTI, M. E. Performance-oriented assessment of mobility problems in elderly patients. TINETTI, M. E. Performance-oriented assessment of mobility problems in elderly patients. , v. 34, no. 2, pp. 119-126, 1986.

Score Interpretation

High Risk (≤ 18 points)
High risk of falls. Implementation of rigorous preventive measures, ambulation assistance, and rehabilitation is recommended.

Moderate Risk (19-23 points)
Moderate risk. The patient may need environmental adaptations and prevention guidance, as well as occasional supervision.

Low Risk (≥ 24 points)
Low risk of falls. Continue monitoring and encourage the patient's maintenance of mobility.
